title: Extraction of CRISPR-targeted sequences from the metagenome
author: Sugimoto, Nishimura, et al.
materials: Timing: 1–12 h (Varies strongly depending on library)

steps.title: Assemble metagenome contigs with SPAdes
steps.instruction: Run SPAdes on the pre‑processed FASTQ file, skipping error‑correction, with 8 threads and 100 GB memory: `spades.py -t 8 -m 100 --meta --only-assembler --12 ecc.fastq.gz -o <spades_output_dir>`. Then assign unique identifiers to each contig to avoid later conflicts: `cd <spades_output_dir>`; generate a random 12‑byte hex string `id=$(openssl rand -hex 12)`; rename contigs with `awk -v id=${id} '/^>/ {n++; print ">contig_"id"_"n";} !/^>/ {print}' scaffolds.fasta > scaffolds.renamed.fasta`. Optionally remove contigs shorter than 1 kb to reduce file size and ensure sufficient disk space for intermediate files.

substeps.instruction: Generate random ID and rename contigs.

steps.title: Detect and extract CRISPR direct repeats
steps.instruction:
Run CRISPRDetect on the renamed contigs to discover consensus direct repeats: `CRISPRDetect.pl -q 0 -f scaffolds.renamed.fasta -o crispr_detect_output -array_quality_score_cutoff 27`. Extract repeat regions from the resulting GFF and convert to FASTA: `grep 'repeat_region' crispr_detect_output.gff | cut -f 9 | tr ';' '
' | egrep '^Note=' | cut -f 2 -d '=' | awk '{n++; printf(">DR_%i
%s
", n, $0)}' > crispr_dr.fasta`. Merge DR files from all assemblies, assign new unique IDs, and deduplicate: `cat {all_crispr_dr_fasta_files} > merged_crispr_dr.fasta`; `awk '/^>/ {n++; print ">dr_"n; } !/^>/ {print}' merged_crispr_dr.fasta > merged_crispr_dr.renamed.fasta`; `cd-hit-est -S 1 -c 1 -i merged_crispr_dr.renamed.fasta -o merged_crispr_dr.repr.fasta`.

substeps.instruction: Merge, rename, and deduplicate repeat sequences.

steps.title: Extract CRISPR spacers from reads
steps.instruction: Filter pre‑processed reads for those containing the identified direct repeats: `bbduk.sh in=ecc.fastq.gz ref=merged_crispr_dr.repr.fasta outm=dr_containing_reads.fastq.gz interleaved=t k=21 hdist=1 rename=t10`. Mask the direct repeats in those reads: `bbduk.sh in=dr_containing_reads.fastq.gz ref=merged_crispr_dr.repr.fasta kmask=R k=19 hdist=1 out=dr_masked.fastq mink=1511`. Extract spacers with the provided Python script: `<path_to_virome_scripts>/pipeline_scripts/extract_spacers.py -s <sample_name> dr_masked.fastq > spacers.fasta`. (The script can be tuned to output shorter sequences with the `-s` and `-l` options.) Merge spacer FASTA files from all samples, assign unique identifiers, and remove redundancy: `cat {all_spacer_fasta_files} > all_spacers.fasta`; `awk '/^>/ {sub(/^[[[:space:]]]+/, ""); n++; printf(">spacer_"n"\t"$0);} !/^>/ {print}' all_spacers.fasta > all_spacers.renamed.fasta`; `cd-hit-est -T 8 -M 10000 -d 0 -sf 1 -s 0.9 -c 0.98 -i all_spacers.renamed.fasta -o all_spacers.repr.fasta`.

substeps.instruction: Extract reads containing direct repeats with bbduk.
Mask direct repeats in those reads.
Run extract_spacers.py to obtain spacer sequences.
Merge, rename, and deduplicate spacer sequences.

steps.title: Optional downstream sequence analysis
steps.instruction: Perform additional computational analyses on the representative direct‑repeat and spacer FASTA files: (1) Cluster sequences to ensure redundancy removal (already done with cd‑hit‑est). (2) Assess genomic completeness by detecting terminal redundancy or inverted terminal repeats using the provided utilities `utils/circular_contigs.py` and `utils/inverted_repeat_contigs.py`. (3) Classify CRISPR‑Cas systems by conducting a high‑sensitivity protein homology search based on hidden Markov models.

substeps.instruction: Run circular_contigs.py and inverted_repeat_contigs.py for completeness checks.
Execute HMM‑based homology searches to classify CRISPR‑Cas systems.
